classification_rule:
Written because a summary assembled from memory is where selective reporting creeps in. Each
row names the artifact it came from, so any line can be checked, and the classification rule is
applied mechanically rather than by recollection:

rows.item: Unconditional harm reduction (B13)
rows.result: 28.2% undefended -> 10.4%; task-alone base rate 1/309
rows.caveat: population changed from the 42.3%->12.5% figure, so levels are not comparable

rows.item: Provenance reaches classes content-only cannot (pre-registered)
rows.result: additive fabrication 0/72 -> 37/72 (p=1e-11); fabricated preferences 0/48 -> 27/48 (p=1e-08); legitimate-instruction false flags 14/40 -> 2/40

rows.item: Provenance is cheaper than the stack it replaces
rows.result: B13 0.1s vs B12 0.15s per admitted memory

rows.item: Bespoke signals beat every published detector on memory poisoning
rows.result: own attacks: B13 46.1% vs deberta 14.1%; baselines 3-15% on note-shaped poisoning

rows.item: Our false-positive rates far below the baselines' on ordinary memory
rows.result: B13 1/1088, B15 1/1088 vs deberta 8/1088, Llama Guard 23/1088

rows.item: Working-set discipline (the round's main methodological contribution)
rows.result: 1117/2628 = 42.5% of instances both subvert an undefended agent and implement their label; per-population floors break CI on drift

rows.item: AgentPoison published records function once probed correctly
rows.result: 0/6 -> 3/6 working, task-alone base rate 0; four prior readings were measurement error

rows.item: memory_worm regeneration
rows.result: 33% mechanism-correct -> 90.0% by an out-of-loop judge; undefended harm 83.3% at 60% retrieval -> 3.3% with B13

rows.item: Corroboration fix lifts every founding family
rows.result: sleeper 0% -> 37%, MPBench 11% -> 46%, MINJA 13% -> 33%, DSRM 17% -> 30%, FARMA 74% -> 87%; aggregate own-attack recall 46.1% -> 59.7%, discrimination +46.1 -> +52.2
rows.caveat: costs 7.5% ordinary-benign FPR, all of it on untrusted channels

rows.item: Corroboration costs nothing on user-authored content
rows.result: legitimate standing instructions 0/40, named-party preferences 0/6, confirmed-human 0/20 in the user_turn channel with evidence live

rows.item: Union configurations beat both components at no extra FPR (descriptive)
rows.result: B17 own 51.2% vs B13 46.1% / B14 41.2%; adds no ordinary-benign false positive
rows.caveat: hold-out-informed; not a clean estimate; and 'no extra FPR' holds on ordinary memory only -- on hold-out 4's matched benign the union excludes 42/262 vs B13's 31 and B14's 24 (R7-12)

rows.item: Matched operating points close most of the baseline gap
rows.result: deberta +36.9 vs B14 +34.1; was a 17-point gap at shipped thresholds, now 2.8
rows.caveat: the baseline still leads on that corpus; and every scorer was calibrated on a 'dev' set that proved to be near-copies of hold-out 3's own benign half (round 7, R7-1), so this is a symmetric but HOLD-OUT-CALIBRATED comparison

rows.item: Multi-hop is not a reasoning ceiling
rows.result: every agent 80-87% correct under the LLM judge; Gemini 60.0% strict, below phi3:mini's 65.0%; the oracle ceiling is NLI strictness
rows.caveat: this corrects a claim this project had published

rows.item: Three frozen hold-outs with pre-registration and digest verification
rows.result: 1,258 + 1,200 + 1,000 human-authored attacks; hold-out 3 adds 995 MATCHED benign from the same platforms

rows.item: Matched-benign false-positive rates are very high
rows.result: B18 54.9%, B14 54.5%, B13 33.5% against 0.09% on ordinary memory
rows.caveat: every FPR previously published used benign text unlike the attack distribution; detection cannot fix this (B19 failed, 32.44) but neutralisation addresses the regime on a different axis at zero false-positive cost (32.46)

rows.item: Three of five pre-registered predictions failed
rows.result: P2 (B18 beats B14 by 5pts) failed at +0.4; P4 (baselines degrade most) failed backwards; P5 (nothing above 85%) failed for four configs

rows.item: The recall ranking inverts once FPR is counted
rows.result: B14/B17/B18 reach 92.7-93.1% recall by flagging >half of benign; their discrimination is the worst of the configurations tested

rows.item: My labelling-artifact hypothesis was mostly wrong
rows.result: 82.7% of the corpus is benign-as-a-memory; filtering moves B18 only 54.9% -> 49.0%, about 6 of 55 points

rows.item: The content detector is the false-positive source, not provenance
rows.result: content-only 43.0% on DEV in-the-wild benign; corroboration adds 2 of 200
rows.caveat: my earlier reading blamed corroboration and was wrong; and the 'DEV' items were hold-out 3 prompts under a different wrapper (R7-1), so this is a hold-out measurement

rows.item: 'B13 is the recommendation' was wrong unqualified
rows.result: on working attacks B14 STRICTLY dominates B13 on the clean hold-out, 40/64 vs 8/64, +32/-0, p=5e-10; B13's 12.5% there was unreported

rows.item: B14's hold-out gap is half composition, half inherited from deberta
rows.result: 36.6-point gap narrows to 20.6 on working attacks (p=0.0001); B14 agrees with deberta 90.1% on external corpora and degrades worse than it across corpora

rows.item: The union configurations cannot reach a low false-positive regime
rows.result: B17's FPR on hold-out 3 cannot go below 33.5% and B18's below 35.0% at ANY threshold, because both exclude whenever B13 excludes; they also leave 6.2 and 9.2 points of discrimination unused at their shipped points
rows.caveat: so the recommendation is now conditioned on the false-positive budget rather than naming one configuration

rows.item: The first pre-registered adaptive test was underpowered and I had to revise its design
rows.result: 1/38 vs 0/38 at p=1.0: one control event caps the p-value regardless of the true effect. Superseded by the powered re-run, but the original rule did fail

rows.item: Exfiltration regeneration only half worked
rows.result: 38% -> 68.8% out-of-loop, but generator acceptance 38.1% equals the unguided rate, so the spec did not improve authoring

rows.item: My own errors this round
rows.result: AgentPoison trigger error a 5th time (caught by my own new guard test); rejection-memory dev fit measured the wrong distribution; orphan script killed the pipeline runner; a guard test matched its own docstring; corroboration left inert in every published table; the user_turn arm computed but never reported; B12 omitted from the table testing it. Round 7 added two more: a disjointness check that compared wrapped strings (R7-1), and a new guard test whose callee persisted its fit and overwrote the ledger radius on disk (caught by git status, restored, and now prevented by a session-wide read-only check)

rows.item: Five of seven founding families are weakly detected content-only
rows.result: DSRM, MPBench, MINJA, MemoryGraft 11-32%; sleeper 0% before the corroboration fix
rows.caveat: these are floors; see evidence_round6.json

rows.item: Adaptive evasion resolved (the open item of every prior round)
rows.result: 32/130 = 24.6% stateless control -> 1/130 = 0.8% with the ledger; paired +0/-31, p=9.31e-10 over 31 discordant pairs, 20 families
rows.caveat: radius was pre-registered but the SEED RULE was revised after the first test failed; and the 0.90 radius carries a 29.7% ledger-poisoning blast radius against 0.7% at 0.97, so the finding is the trade, not a solved problem

rows.item: Exfiltration is now a TESTED mechanism
rows.result: deterministic structural gates added after the judge was shown to pass instances with no recipient; regenerated set scores 87.5% out-of-loop (was 68.8%), 16/16 pass the gate, and all three agent families give 0/16 harm -- they address the legitimate counterparty and only RESTATE the attacker's directive
rows.caveat: a negative result about the attack class against 7-8B assistants, not a benchmark defect; the deterministic recipient column overstates adoption and the judge is the accurate instrument

rows.item: B18 with evidence is the best configuration on this benchmark's own threat
rows.result: own attacks 519/804 = 64.6% at 81/1054 = 7.7% ordinary-benign FPR, discrimination +56.9 against B13's +52.2 and B12's +43.2; the corroboration arm had never been run for B18
rows.caveat: the entire false-positive cost falls on untrusted channels: 0/40, 0/6, 0/20 in the user_turn condition. SUPERSEDED as a recommendation (R7-13): on clean hold-out 4 B18 matches B13's recall exactly and adds false positives (16.0% vs 11.8%); the lead here was measured on populations B18 was selected after reading

rows.item: The memory-shape gate failed: the FPR problem is not fixable this way
rows.result: B19 = gate + B13 gives attacks 83.2% and benign 64.2%, discrimination +21.1 against B13's +45.8; a structural-rules-only variant gives +45.3, i.e. no gain. On an in-the-wild prompt corpus the benign and malicious halves are structurally indistinguishable, so no shape pre-filter can separate them
rows.caveat: reported as a failed attempt rather than retained; hold-out 3 has now been scored five times and only the first was pre-registered

rows.item: NEUTRALISATION resolves the one regime detection could not
rows.result: hold-out 3 attack compliance 34.0% -> 14.7%, paired +5/-34, p=2.4e-06, with no significant change in benign information use; nothing is excluded so the false-positive rate is zero by construction
rows.caveat: HOLD-OUT 3 USE 7 OF 7 (not an independent estimate; replicated cleanly on hold-out 5, 37.4% -> 18.3%); the active ingredient is recency alone; v2/v3/v5 are indistinguishable at n=120 given a ~5-point noise floor, and the frame this project first built is actively harmful

rows.item: Prediction calibration demonstrated, not asserted
rows.result: 5/5 pre-registered predictions held on an unmeasured target (B17/B18 on hold-out 2), with intervals committed before the run
rows.caveat: it does not un-fail the three that failed in the first pre-registration

rows.item: New best on hold-out 2
rows.result: B18 reaches 72.7% against B14's 54.2%, at 2/1054 ordinary-benign false positives
rows.caveat: B17/B18 postdate the hold-out results that informed their design, so this is not a clean generalisation estimate

rows.item: Every past error's guard PROVEN by mutation testing
rows.result: 35/35 guards fail when their error is reintroduced and pass again once restored
rows.caveat: establishing it exposed that four of eight guards had been decoration, plus CRLF shell scripts, a guard passing on exit 127, and the harness corrupting what it measured twice

rows.item: My 'instability inherited from deberta' attribution was imprecise
rows.result: removing the feature WIDENS the cross-corpus gap (+32.9 to +46.6) and costs recall everywhere, hold-out 2 collapsing 59.8% to 40.7%; the gap is a property of the fused weights and the feature is load-bearing
rows.caveat: still consistent with B18: a fusion can under-use a feature it contains, which is a different claim from that feature causing the instability

rows.item: The neutralisation frame I originally built is actively harmful
rows.result: v1_prefix raises attack compliance 6.7 points and costs 10 points of benign utility; the earlier 'partial, 49/150 -> 38/150' reading came from a hold-out sample that flattered it

rows.item: Recommendation conditioned on threat and false-positive budget, on clean hold-outs
rows.result: memory poisoning: B13 + evidence (hold-out 4: 50.3% at 11.8% untrusted / 0% user_turn; B17/B18 dominated there); injection: B17 at ~10% FPR (hold-out 5: 90.1% at 10.2%); neutralisation as a zero-exclusion layer (halves compliance on hold-out 5); the ledger for retry-capable attackers
rows.caveat: supersedes 32.42/32.45, which named B18 for memory poisoning on hold-out-informed numbers

rows.item: The hold-out 3 development set was the hold-out (R7-1)
rows.result: 382/400 'dev' benign items are hold-out 3 prompts verbatim under a different memory wrapper (393 near-copies); 647/648 of the earlier jailbreak snapshot are near-copies of hold-out 3 attacks. The disjointness check compared wrapped strings
rows.caveat: the matched-FPR comparison and frontier are hold-out-calibrated; the per-rule FPR attribution was a hold-out measurement; B19 was fitted on near-copies and still failed, so that negative stands. Guard proven by mutation (dev_holdout_overlap)

rows.item: Founding families re-measured under B18 + evidence (never done before)
rows.result: B18 with the owner's conversation: agentpoison 64.9%, minja 40.4%, farma 87.0%, memorygraft 34.2%, dsrm 30.4%, mpbench 47.8%, sleeper_memory_poisoning 36.8% at 81/1054 ordinary-benign FPR; no model re-run, union identity verified item by item
rows.caveat: mixed: MemoryGraft and DSRM stay near 30% even at the best configuration measured, and B18 adds nothing over B17 on any founding family

rows.item: B17/B18 have clean hold-out estimates (was OPEN)
rows.result: hold-out 5 (pre-registered, scored once): B17 90.1% recall at 10.2% matched-benign FPR, B18 90.1% at 11.0%; hold-out 4: both 50.3% at 16.0% untrusted / 1.5% user_turn
rows.caveat: B18 adds nothing over B17 on either hold-out; hold-out 5 has only 131 attacks (+/-8 points)

rows.item: The 33-55% matched-benign FPR regime does not generalise (pre-registered)
rows.result: on hold-out 5's matched benign B17 10.2%, B18 11.0%, B13 5.1% against 54.8% / 54.9% / 33.5% on hold-out 3
rows.caveat: the earlier 'unfixable by detection' reading was largely a property of hold-out 3's jailbreak-community benign prompts; it stands as a fact about that corpus

rows.item: Provenance reaches memory poisoning on the first memory-poisoning hold-out (was OPEN)
rows.result: hold-out 4 (new author family, new owner, scored once): B13 50.3% vs B14 20.4% (p=1e-14), content-only B12 1.9%, deberta@dev 0.0%, llama_guard@dev 0.6%
rows.caveat: costs 11.8% benign FPR on the untrusted channel (0% on user_turn); note-shaped families only -- the author inverted both instruction-shaped families, which were withdrawn before freezing

rows.item: Neutralisation halves compliance on a clean injection hold-out at zero exclusions
rows.caveat: framing costs 2.2 points of benign information use on dev (n.s.); on hold-out 4's note-shaped attacks it does almost nothing

rows.item: The pre-registered PRIMARY composition test failed on the clean hold-out
rows.result: B12 exclude + neutralise vs B12 exclude: 20 -> 15 of 131, p=0.23; and B18 exclusion alone (4.6% harm at 11.0%) beat B12+neutralise (11.5% at 2.6%)
rows.caveat: the dev result (23.3% at 1.2% vs 32.0% at 7.0%) did not generalise: where detectors reach 90% recall, neutralisation is a trade along the FPR axis, not a dominating configuration

rows.item: Round-7 pre-registration scored mechanically
rows.result: 34/41 held (CALIBRATED); failed: H5-3, H5-6, H5-7, H6-6, H7-6, H7-7, R-4
rows.caveat: failures stay in the table; one interval failed by 0.1 point and counts as failed

rows.item: The #8 lead (unions without B13's content detector) failed on dev
rows.result: B20 56.1% vs B17 64.4% on own attacks at the same FPR; dominated in both beds
rows.caveat: B13's content detector excludes no ordinary benign but catches attacks B14 misses

rows.item: Exfiltration authoring fixed: the instruction, not the author (#10)
rows.result: accepted (gates AND judge): qwen spec 1/40, qwen few-shot 11/40, gemini spec 2/40, gemini few-shot 7/40
rows.caveat: n=40 per generator; only the spec-only vs few-shot gap is claimed

rows.item: Round-7 measurement and description errors found and corrected
rows.result: R7-3 an artifact naming the wrong neutralisation frame; R7-8 leading probes (task-alone 66/157 -> 7/157 after the fix); R7-10 the published harm study used FIXED tasks while a summary said per-instance
rows.caveat: each corrected in place; R7-8 and R7-10 are guarded

rows.item: Neutralisation on this project's own attacks (Phase B)
rows.result: harm 28.8% raw -> 24.6% framed; B13 9.1% -> B13+frame 6.5%
rows.caveat: both arms re-run in one session (noise floor ~5 points)

rows.item: Neutralisation on a stronger agent (Phase B)
rows.result: gemini 50.0% -> 13.3% (+36.7 pts) vs qwen +20.0 on the same 60 items
rows.caveat: n=60; differences of a few points are noise

rows.item: Ledger radius swept against its denial-of-service surface (Phase B)
rows.result: radius 0.95 keeps the adaptive-evasion effect with a ledger-poisoning blast radius of 6.4% (0.90: 29.7%)
rows.caveat: selection rule fixed before the sweep

rows.item: Every phase verified end to end
rows.result: 3,466 tests passed, 32 skipped, 0 failed across phases 3-17, attribution and the cross-cutting suite; phase 3 and phase 5 datasets intact and needing no regeneration

rows.item: The harm judge agrees only weakly with a human annotator
rows.result: harm: 60% agreement, kappa 0.2, 16 misses vs 0 false alarms (n=40); compliance: 75%, kappa 0.5
rows.caveat: one annotator who said YES on 80/100 items; the disagreement is one-sided (judges stricter). Harm LEVELS carry this caveat; reductions are more robust (same judge both arms); detection and FPR results do not use these judges

rows.item: A second independent human annotator
rows.result: needed to separate 'the judges are strict' from 'one annotator's threshold is lower', and to measure human-to-human agreement

rows.item: The run-to-run noise floor is measured, not assumed
rows.result: three independent runs: raw compliance [61, 62, 63] of 120 (SD 0.83 pts), framed [36, 40, 39] (SD 1.73), undefended harm [87, 89, 94] of 309 (SD 1.17)
rows.caveat: dev only; the ~5-point floor used throughout is conservative

rows.item: A better harm judge, chosen on half the human labels and tested on the other half
rows.result: current judge TEST kappa 0.239; adopted J2_gemini_original TEST kappa 0.773
rows.caveat: agreement is with ONE annotator; harm levels are re-measured with the adopted judge BESIDE the original, never in place of it

rows.item: Instruction-shaped memory poisoning only partly testable on a clean hold-out
rows.result: hold-out 7 (base-model author): standing instructions 23/40 valid, conditional backdoors 3/40 -- conditional backdoors remain effectively untested
rows.caveat: the safety-tuned author inverted these families (hold-out 4); the base model writes standing instructions but not dormant triggers

rows.item: The false-positive finding replicates on a second independent corpus (hold-out 6)
rows.result: B17 77.6% recall at 2.2% matched-benign FPR (500 / 1,000, SPML)
rows.caveat: LLM-authored corpus; 3,728 near-copies dropped before freezing

rows.item: The failed composition test holds when powered (hold-out 6)
rows.result: B12 exclusion + neutralise-the-rest vs B12 alone: 246 -> 227 of 500, p=0.023
rows.caveat: adds nothing on top of B18; it helps a weak detector, not a strong one; holds at its pre-registered alpha but NOT after Holm correction across the round's nine significance predictions (adjusted p~0.07)

rows.item: Two defects of B18 found on hold-outs
rows.result: its deberta hard rule cost 16.3% FPR on hold-out 6 and excluded 3.7% of hold-out 7's user_turn benign notes (ignores channel trust)
rows.caveat: the recommendation for injection-shaped text is now B17, not B18; any B18 fix is hold-out-informed

rows.item: Hold-out 7: contradiction rule adds nothing; framing backfired on instruction attacks
rows.result: B13c +0 on contradiction attacks; framing raised compliance on instruction-shaped attacks (+5 points)
rows.caveat: hold-out 7's working subset is not reportable (probe base rate 28% > the 20% rule)

rows.item: Usefulness cost of the neutralisation frame on benign memories: no significant cost
rows.caveat: 300 benign notes, agent qwen2.5:7b; largest loss direct_question +5.0 points (p=0.082), one LLM judge

rows.item: Adaptive evasion vs neutralisation (descriptive only)
rows.result: 6/31 initially-caught seeds evaded within 5 rewrites
rows.caveat: conditional on an initial catch; vs 32/130 stateless reference, Fisher p=0.64

rows.item: Adaptive evasion vs corroboration: brittle -- above the stateless reference
rows.result: 22/48 initially-caught seeds evaded within 5 rewrites
rows.caveat: conditional on an initial catch; vs 32/130 stateless reference, Fisher p=0.0096

rows.item: Harm study re-judged with the human-validated judge (PARTIAL)
rows.result: undefended, all items: J0_current 32.0%; J2_gemini_original 58.3% | stratum n=120: J0_current: undefended 34.2%, B13 5.0%; J2_gemini_original: undefended 46.7%, B13 8.3%
rows.caveat: identical full-text answers; original figures stand beside it; 166 Gemini verdicts outstanding (daily quota), stratum = authority_impersonation, conditional_backdoor, exfiltration_instruction, memory_worm, policy_revocation, preference_hijack

rows.item: Harm with a stronger agent (Gemini): B13 still cuts it
rows.result: undefended 36.0% vs qwen 31.0%; B13 14.0%
rows.caveat: seeded 100 of the 309 harm-study instances (seed 41); an estimate; B13 vs undefended p=4.8e-07; Gemini vs qwen undefended p=0.46; original harm judge (levels likely under-estimates, Section 13A)

rows.item: Stronger-agent framing effect, all 120 dev items
rows.result: Gemini +32.5 vs qwen +20.8 points
rows.caveat: extension for precision, not the pre-registered test

rows.item: Hold-out 6: the attacks that work are harder to detect (direction is corpus-specific)
rows.result: B13 37.2% full vs 28.6% working; B14 77.4% full vs 68.4% working; B17 77.6% full vs 68.4% working; B18 98.6% full vs 98.6% working
rows.caveat: 294/500 working, task-alone base rate 33/500 (under the 20% rule); full-population recall overstates protection; B18 holds only through its 16.3%-FPR deberta rule; on hold-outs 4 and 5 the working attacks are EASIER for B13 (~+10 points) -- Table 21

rows.item: EXPLORATORY: the ledger would block most corroboration evasions
rows.caveat: post-hoc upper bound on dev; the composed adaptive run (B13 + ledger) is not yet measured

rows.item: The ledger closes corroboration's adaptive weakness (pre-registered)
rows.caveat: dev only; ledger cost = 6.4% blast radius at 0.95 (dev); B18 + ledger not measured (~40 s per B18 decision)

rows.item: Phase 10 risk-weighted retrieval: cross-guard corroboration demotes poison (first evaluation)
rows.result: exposure 88 -> 82 of 309 vs the fixed gate, p=0.031; benign displacement 0.0 points
rows.caveat: narrow: admission signals fired on the poison in 28/309 instances; dev only; not robust to a family-wide Holm correction

rows.item: Phase 6's fixed-gate retrieval guard barely changes what reaches the agent
rows.result: exposure 89 -> 88 of 309 (p=1); lexical divergence positive for only 120/6180 candidates
rows.caveat: pre-registered R-4 FAILED

rows.item: Phase 10 risk-weighted monitoring (forensic ordering) not evaluated
rows.result: built and unit-tested; orders a human triage queue
rows.caveat: no outcome this benchmark measures
